newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Budapest milling wheat limit-up, feed wheat down.
newsitem.headline: Budapest milling wheat limit-up, feed wheat down.

text.p: Fears of a low quality wheat crop pushed milling wheat prices limit-up on the Budapest Commodity Exchange while feed wheat prices went limit-down for the same reason, traders said.
"The market thinks that out of the total five million tonnes wheat crop expected, only two million tonnes will be of milling quality," said Sandor Torok of Agrokont.

Milling wheat prices rose the daily allowed 400 forints per tonne for all positions except September and January, which rose 200 and 300 forints, respectively. The September 1998 contract opened at 26,200 forints.
Torok said, however, that the rising trend of milling wheat prices could end as current spot prices were already comparable with import prices.
"Mills are already said to be considering imports," he said.
Euro wheat, which currently trades for all months between August 1998 and January 1999, went limit-up for all maturities in sympathy with milling wheat.
Feed wheat fell the limit for all maturities and Torok said the the market expected some three million tonnes of feed wheat from this year's harvest, of which hardly any could be exported.
Feed barley rose the limit for all positions on lack of supply but Torok said on the longer term prices were likely to stabilise.
Maize futures were mostly steady but Torok said prices will have to come down sooner or later due to expectations of a good crop.
"Traders are now trying to keep prices high so they can open selling positions later on, but large amounts of maize will hit the market and drive prices down," he said.
Total grains futures turnover rose to 1,256 lots or 577.9 million forints from Tuesday's 425 contracts or 179.3 million forints.
